skill.name: browser-automation
skill.description: Browser automation guidance for WebDriver workflows, including web testing, form automation, screenshots, web scraping, performance checks, recipes, and driver management for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge.
skill.summary: Automates browser workflows with WebDriver, recipes, screenshots, and performance checks.
skill.author: EmilLindfors

security_audit.summary: Most static network and external-command matches are documentation examples, installer help text, or Markdown backticks and were dismissed. Real risks remain around broad Read/Bash/Write permissions, local screenshot and config writes, authenticated scraping, and browser-context JavaScript execution. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash and Write from allowed-tools unless required, and require explicit user confirmation for setup scripts or local writes.
Add clear consent, scope, and data-handling guidance before extracting protected page HTML or running custom scripts.

remediation.issue: Local file writes for screenshots and Claude config
remediation.suggestion: Use user-provided output paths, avoid shared /tmp defaults for sensitive captures, and back up configuration before modification.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks are slow and hard to repeat. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through WebDriver automation.
actual_capabilities: Navigate pages and control Chrome, Firefox, and Edge sessions through WebDriver.
Find elements, click controls, enter text, and submit forms.
Capture screenshots, page source, text, attributes, and current URLs.
Run performance, memory, resource, and console log checks.
Create and execute reusable automation recipes with parameters and retries.
Start, stop, list, and health-check managed browser drivers.
limitations: Requires a compatible WebDriver and local browser installation.
Cannot bypass CAPTCHAs, access controls, or site terms.
Browser actions may expose authenticated page data to the active AI session.
Setup scripts may modify Claude Desktop configuration when run.

use_cases.title: Regression Test Web Flows
use_cases.description: Automate login, form submission, navigation, and visual checks across supported browsers.

use_cases.title: Collect Structured Web Data
use_cases.description: Extract page text, product lists, tables, and links from approved sites using repeatable selectors.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Page Performance
use_cases.description: Measure load timing, memory usage, resource behavior, and console errors during realistic browser sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], wait for [selector], then report the page title, current URL, and visible status text.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a test account to fill [form name] on [URL], submit it, and capture validation messages or success text.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Approved Data
prompt_templates.prompt: From [approved URL], collect [fields] from each item, follow pagination safely, and stop after [limit] pages.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Performance Across Browsers
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a multi-browser performance audit for [URL], compare load metrics, console errors, memory usage, and screenshot evidence.

output_examples.input: Check a landing page after deployment.
output: Loaded the requested URL and confirmed the expected page title.
Found the target header and primary call to action.
No blocking console errors were observed during the check.

output_examples.input: Test a contact form with invalid and valid data.
output: Invalid data produced the expected validation messages.
Valid test data submitted successfully and showed a confirmation message.
A screenshot was captured for review in the chosen output path.

output_examples.input: Compare page performance for two versions.
output: Version B loaded faster on average across the configured iterations.
First contentful paint improved, but one console warning remained.
Memory growth stayed within the expected range during the run.

best_practices: Use test accounts and approved sites for all automation.
Wait for stable elements before clicking or extracting data.
Store credentials outside recipes and clear sessions after authenticated work.
anti_patterns: Do not automate sites without permission or against their terms.
Do not save screenshots or page source containing sensitive data to shared paths.
Do not rely on fixed sleeps when an element wait is available.

faq.question: Which browsers are supported?
faq.answer: The skill documents workflows for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge through compatible WebDriver drivers.

faq.question: Does it install browser drivers?
faq.answer: No. It expects WebDriver tools to be installed, and setup scripts only help check or configure the environment.

faq.question: Can it bypass CAPTCHAs?
faq.answer: No. The examples state that CAPTCHAs should be disabled only in authorized test environments.

faq.question: Can it scrape authenticated pages?
faq.answer: It can guide authenticated workflows, but users must have permission and protect any sensitive data collected.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports screenshot workflows when the user provides a safe local output path.

faq.question: Is it suitable for performance testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for load timing, console errors, memory checks, and resource monitoring.
